results.question: How much is the monthly fee on the everyday account and how do I avoid paying it?
results.answer:
The Everyday Account has a monthly fee of KES 250. You don't pay it in a month when either of these applies:

- **Salary paid in:** The KES 250 monthly fee is waived for any month in which your salary is paid into your Kaskazi Everyday Account. Transfers from your own other accounts, cash deposits and mobile money don't count as salary.
- **Average balance of KES 50,000 or more:** Kaskazi Bank adds up the balance in your Kaskazi Everyday Account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month. A balance that dips below KES 50,000 on some days can still qualify.

You only need one waiver to apply.

results.question: If I break my fixed deposit early do I lose my money?
results.answer:
No, you don't lose your deposit. If you break a Kaskazi Fixed Deposit early, you lose half of the interest earned so far. Kaskazi Bank pays you the other half, after withholding tax, together with the full amount you deposited. You never lose any of the money you deposited by breaking a Kaskazi Fixed Deposit early.

For example, on a KES 500,000 12-month deposit at 9.5% broken after 151 days, you receive KES 508,351.54: your KES 500,000 plus KES 8,351.54 interest after tax.

Please note that you can't take out part of a Kaskazi Fixed Deposit. To get any money out before maturity, you must break the whole deposit. If you'd like to start the process, I can help you in the app.

results.question: why cant i withdraw more than 20k a day from my student acount??

The limit covers all cash withdrawals added together: at Kaskazi Bank ATMs, at other banks' ATMs, at Kaskazi agents and at branches. It can't be raised on a Kaskazi Student Account.

For large payments, pay by transfer or card instead of cash. School fees payments from your Kaskazi account are free. Card payments in shops and online are not cash withdrawals, so they don't count towards the KES 20,000.

results.question: what happens to my student account when I turn 26
results.answer:
When you turn 26, your Kaskazi Student Account becomes a Kaskazi Everyday Account automatically, the month after your 26th birthday. The bank tells you in the app before the change happens. For example, if your 26th birthday is on 14 March 2027, your Kaskazi Student Account becomes a Kaskazi Everyday Account in April 2027.

Your account number, debit card and PIN, balance, standing orders and app login all stay the same. The Kaskazi Everyday Account monthly fee of KES 250 a month applies, unless your salary is paid into the account that month or your average balance for the month is KES 50,000 or more. Your KES 20,000 Student Account limit no longer applies, and the card's standard daily ATM limit of KES 100,000 applies instead.

If you start work, you can ask your employer to pay your salary into this account. In any month your salary is paid in, the KES 250 Everyday Account fee is waived.

results.question: what does 'up to 50 days interest free' actually mean? do I get 50 days on everything I buy with the credit card?
results.answer:
No, not on everything. "Up to 50 days" is the longest period. The number of interest-free days depends on when in the statement period you make the purchase. A purchase made on the first day of a statement period waits the longest before it is due, so it gets the full 50 days. A purchase made on the last day of a statement period gets the fewest days.

For example, with a statement period from 1 May to 31 May and a payment due date of 20 June, a purchase on 1 May gets 50 days, one on 15 May gets 36 days, and one on 31 May gets 20 days.

Two conditions also apply. The interest-free period applies only when you pay your full statement balance by the payment due date. And it does not apply to cash advances.

Your app shows your statement date and your next payment due date, so you can check how many interest-free days a purchase will get.

results.question: how much is the monthly fee on everyday account? and can i avoid paying it
results.answer:
The monthly fee on the Kaskazi Everyday Account is **KES 250**. The Kaskazi Everyday Account has a monthly fee of KES 250.

You can avoid it in either of two ways, and you only need one:

- **Salary paid in:** The KES 250 monthly fee is waived for any month in which your salary is paid into your Kaskazi Everyday Account. Transfers from your own other accounts, cash deposits, mobile money and payments from friends or family don't count as salary.
- **Average balance of KES 50,000 or more:** Kaskazi Bank adds up the balance in your Kaskazi Everyday Account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month. The balance can fall below KES 50,000 on some days and you can still qualify, as long as the average for the whole month is KES 50,000 or more.

The bank checks at the end of each month, so you pay nothing for any month that qualifies.

results.question: how is the personal loan interest worked out, is it linked to the base rate?
results.answer:
